 Credible is a reputable student loan marketplace to compare many student loan or refinancing offers in one dashboard. Amy DeYoung, Special to USA TODAY Sat 7 November 2026 at 9:52 am GMT-6 12 min read If you're looking for private student loans to cover college costs, a loan marketplace like Credible can help. Loan marketplaces let borrowers prequalify with multiple lenders at once, so you can easily compare interest rates, repayment terms and other loan terms. Credible is a reputable lending marketplace with an A+ Better Business Bureau rating, known for competitive interest rates, no origination fees and lower credit score requirements than many competitors. Keep reading to learn more about Credible's service, interest rates and whether it's worth it for borrowers shopping for private student loans. 
 Credible overview 
 Credible isn't a traditional lender. Instead, it's a loan marketplace where lenders for everything from student loans to auto loans to student loan refinancing compete. Credible shows you prequalified rates, letting you shop multiple lenders at once with only a soft pull on your credit score.

 Find your education financing with Credible 
 Student loan options 
 Credible matches borrowers with a wide variety of loans, including auto and home insurance loans. Here are its student loan options: 
 Undergraduate loans 
 Credible's private student loans can cover up to 100% of the cost of college minus financial aid for eligible students. Depending on your credit score and other financial requirements, you may need a co-signer to qualify or get better interest rates. 
 Graduate loans 
 In addition to undergraduate loans, you can find graduate school loans through Credible's marketplace. Credible also offers specific private student loans for some fields of study, such as medical and law school. 
 Parent loans 
 Some Credible lenders let parents or a creditworthy adult borrow money in their own name, rather than as a co-signer. This option helps parents whose students' financial aid doesn't bridge the gap between what they qualify for and what they need to pay for school. Not all Credible lenders offer parent loans, but most do, allowing parents to qualify for potentially lower interest rates than federal student loans, especially if the parent has a stable income and strong credit. 
 Story continues Student loan refinancing 
 If you're already in student loan debt but want a better rate, Credible can help you shop for a lower interest rate and ease your loan's financial burden. Fixed and variable rates are available for both undergraduate and graduate student loans. Most require a minimum credit score of 665 to 680, though some partner lenders didn't disclose a set requirement. 
 Learn more: I refinanced my student loans. Here's how I knew it was worth it 
 Interest rates, fees and discounts 
 Fixed vs. variable rates 
 When borrowing through Credible lender partners, you can choose fixed or variable rates with most lenders. Fixed rates stay the same throughout the loan's lifetime, while variable rates usually start fixed but change over time with market conditions. 
 At the time of writing, Credible works with lenders with fixed rates ranging from 1.99% to 17.99% APR for undergraduate students. Student loan refinancing rates range from 3.95% to 10.99%, with an average APR of 6.41% for 10-year loans for borrowers with credit scores between 720 and 779. 
 Available discounts 
 With autopay, some Credible lenders knock 0.25 to 0.50 percentage points off your interest rate. Autopay will automatically withdraw the payments from your account each month when your student loan payments become due. 
 Fees 
 Since Credible itself isn't a loan lender, but a loan marketplace, fees vary depending on the specific lender you opt for. Credible doesn't charge origination fees or prepayment penalties, but its lenders may include extra fees, so always check for added fees. 
 Repayment 
 Repayment options 
 Private student loan borrowers can choose between several repayment options when searching for a lender through Credible: 
 Immediate repayment: This option means you start making full principal and interest payments in school. While this keeps costs lower over time, it means budgeting for loan payments while in school, which isn't an option for everyone. 
 Interest-only payments: While in school, you can opt to pay only the interest on your loan so the balance doesn't grow while you're getting your degree. 
 Fixed payments: Some of Credible's lenders let you make small, fixed payments, usually around $25 a month, to offset some accrued interest and get you used to monthly payments. 
 Deferred repayment: This option means that you make no payments while in school and start making payments after your grace period ends (usually 6 months after graduation). Interest will still accrue while you're in school, so your balance will be higher when you start paying. 
 Repayment term lengths 
 Most Credible partner lenders offer repayment term lengths of five, seven, 10 or 15 years, though some loans go up to 20 years. You typically can't change the repayment term length unless you refinance, so consider this term carefully. 
 Grace periods 
 A grace period allows you to defer (or not pay temporarily) student loan payments until after you leave school or graduate. Most Credible lenders offer a six-month grace period, but this varies by lender and loan type. For example, some graduate school loan grace periods are longer, with some lenders offering nine to 36 months for graduate, MBA, medical, law and dental school loans. 
 Cosigner release 
 Many Credible partner lenders offer cosigner release options, but borrowers should verify the terms as they vary by lender. Most Credible's partner lenders let borrowers apply for a cosigner release after 12 to 36 on-time payments, provided you meet the lender's income and credit requirements. 
 Eligibility requirements 
 Credit score 
 Credible works with borrowers with a credit score of 580 and higher. The higher your credit score, the easier it is to get approved and the better the interest rates. 
 Income requirements 
 Since Credible is a loan marketplace, income requirements vary by lender. Generally speaking, the higher your income, the better the interest rates you'll receive. Stable income matters, so you may need a cosigner depending on your financial situation and credit score. 
 Cosigner requirements 
 Credible considers several factors when determining a student's eligibility for a student loan or refinancing, and a cosigner can help you secure a better interest rate or improve your chances of qualifying. 
 Cosigners can be anyone from a spouse to a parent to a family friend, and they must have a credit score of 580 or higher. Credible requires a co-signer if you're under the age of majority in your state or an international student. 
 School eligibility 
 When borrowing from Credible, you must be attending an accredited college or university within the United States. If you don't see your school on the application form, select "Other - school not listed." 
 Application process 
 After filling out the FAFSA, borrowers may find that federal loans and scholarships don't cover all their school expenses. To shop around for private student loans, follow these steps. 
 Complete Credible's quick student loan application. Once you've prequalified, you can view preliminary student loan and refinancing offers without a hard pull or ding on your credit. Take time to compare rates from multiple lenders and look at factors like interest rates, fees, repayment options and borrower benefits. Consider adding a cosigner if you're offered high interest rates or a limited selection of loan offers.Once you find an offer you're interested in, fill out the loan application with information such as your Social Security number, school name, loan amount, income and contact information. 
 After you apply for a loan, the lender runs a hard credit inquiry to verify your credit history, which may lower your credit score by a few points. If you're approved, the lender will confirm your school's cost of attendance, then send funds to your school. The school will then disburse the remaining funds to you for other educational expenses, including transportation, school supplies and books. 
 Find your education financing with Credible 
 Customer experience 
 As a student loan marketplace, Credible matches you with lenders. Customer service varies by lender, so weigh this when you consider loan options, as some offer handy mobile apps, 24/7 support and other perks. 
 Credible's customer service includes live chat, which our team found quick, informative and easy to use. You can also call them at 866-540-6005 or email them at support@credible.com . 
 Customer reviews 
 Credible has an outstanding customer rating of 4.8 stars from nearly 10,000 Trustpilot reviewers, with positive reviews highlighting how easy the marketplace is to use to find and secure different lenders. Reviewers praised Credible's help in finding lower interest rates, along with helpful guides and built-in explanations that made the shopping process smoother. Negative reviews pointed out issues with not being prequalified for loans, despite a good (self-reported) credit score. 
 Credible pros and cons 
 Pros: 
 Borrowers can compare student loan offers from multiple lenders at once 
 Generous autopay discounts via some of its lenders—0.25 to 0.50 (double the industry standard) 
 Most of its lenders offer cosigner releases 
 Cons 
 You have to research and read through each lender's specific terms and conditions 
 Not all lenders disclose requirements, such as a minimum credit score 
 You can only view offers from Credible's partner lenders

 Is Credible right for you? 
 Credible may be right for you if: 
 You want help shopping around for an undergraduate student loan: Credible works with a wide network of student loan lenders and allows you to prequalify once, then check what your available rates will be with lenders you qualify for. 
 You're a graduate student in a specialty program: Credible can match you with lenders that offer graduate, medical, law, MBA and dental loans, with more lenient terms, such as longer grace periods and repayment terms. 
 You're a borrower using a cosigner: Most Credible partner lenders allow you to release the cosigner after 12 to 36 months, but having one during the application process can potentially help you access better interest rates. 
 Refinance borrowers: If you're interested in exploring lower rates and want to refinance at least $5,000 to $15,000, Credible may be worth looking into, as it'll help you quickly prequalify and view different refinancing offers. 
 Bottom line 
 Credible is a reputable choice if you want to compare many student loan or refinancing offers in one dashboard. This saves you time and lets you compare multiple lenders easily, so you can find the best repayment terms and rates for your situation without dinging your credit. We found some of the autopay discounts through Credible's partner lenders especially generous, with a few as high as 0.50 percentage points (twice the industry average). 
 Credible's biggest drawback is that it'll only show its partner lenders, and you'll need to review each lender's terms and conditions, such as repayment and cosigner release terms, since they vary by lender. However, this lending marketplace may be worth exploring if you're interested in private student loans or refinancing, so you can shop around before submitting your final application. 
 FAQs 
 Is Credible legit for student loans? 
 Yes, Credible is a legit student loan marketplace that lets you compare different lenders for private student loans and student loan refinancing. It has an A+ BBB rating and a high 4.8-star rating from nearly 10,000 Trustpilot reviewers. 
 What credit score do you need for Credible loans? 
 You need a minimum credit score of 580 to qualify for a loan through Credible's partner lenders, although most require a credit score of at least 665. 
 Does Credible offer student loan refinancing? 
 Yes, Credible's partner lenders offer student loan refinancing for a minimum balance of $5,000 to $15,000, depending on the lender.
